chunks: There is no sahw in the voluntary prayer; whoever has sahw in a voluntary prayer may build upon whatever he wishes.

The sahw applies only to the obligatory prayer. Whoever has sahw in the first two units must repeat the prayer. Whoever doubts in the Maghrib must repeat the prayer. Whoever doubts in the Ghada (morning prayer) must repeat the prayer.

Whoever doubts between the second and third unit, or between the third and fourth unit, should build upon the higher number; and when he performs taslim, he completes what he suspected he had fallen short of.

The two prostrations of sahw are not obligatory upon the one praying except when he stood while he should have been sitting, or sat while he should have been standing, or omitted the tashahhud, or did not know whether he added to his prayer or fell short of it. They are performed after the taslim, in the case of addition or decrease, and in them one says:
'In the name of Allah and by Allah, peace be upon you O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.'

key_terms.البناء على الأكثر: Building upon the more/higher number — a ruling to assume the maximum number of units completed when doubt arises
key_terms.التسليم: Taslim — the concluding salutation ending the formal prayer
key_terms.التشهد: Tashahhud — the seated testimony recited in prayer; its omission triggers the prostrations of sahw
key_terms.السهو: Sahw — inadvertent forgetfulness or doubt during prayer affecting the count of units performed
key_terms.الفريضة: Fardha — obligatory prayer; sahw in farida has prescribed legal consequences
key_terms.النافلة: Nafilah — voluntary/supererogatory prayer; sahw in nafilah has no binding legal consequence
key_terms.سجدتا السهو: The two prostrations of sahw — a remedial ritual act performed after taslim to compensate for specific inadvertent errors in prayer

ai.seo_question: What are the rules of sahw (forgetfulness) in Islamic prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq presents a comprehensive ruling on the jurisprudence of sahw (inadvertent forgetfulness during prayer). It was narrated during the 93rd assembly of al-Saduq in 368 AH and covers three scenarios: voluntary prayers (where sahw has no legal effect), obligatory prayers requiring repetition (when sahw affects the Fatiha units or prayers of fixed units like Maghrib and Fajr), and the remedy of building upon the higher number for doubts between certain units. The hadith also specifies the precise conditions requiring the two prostrations of sahw and the formula for those prostrations.
